the runtime caller credential: every route except /health requires it as `Authorization: Bearer`, because the workload and schedule surfaces start containers, Pods and processes and fire requests on a caller's word. agent-api and meeting-api hold the same value; no spawned workload receives it. Unset, shorter than 32 bytes, or a published placeholder ⇒ the runtime refuses to boot rather than serve the API open. keys.default: (unset — no store backing: in-store workspace mounts are not bound)
keys.description: what backs the agent workspace store on the substrate — a host path or named volume (docker backend), the PVC claim name (k8s backend); the process backend shares the filesystem and needs none. The RUNTIME's own value: a workload spec's VEXA_WORKSPACE_MOUNT_* keys are discarded, and this is injected into every spec that declares a mount set

where the workspace store sits inside a workload (agent-api's VEXA_WORKSPACES_DIR). Every mount a spec declares must sit strictly under it, or the create is refused (400); on the process backend it is also the root the POSIX tenant isolation seals

keys.default: (unset — no out-of-store mount source is served)
keys.description: comma-separated absolute host paths, outside the workspace store, that a workload's mount set may name as a mount source; any other source is refused. Compose and Helm set it to agent-api's separately managed _global tier when an operator configures one
grace (s) a stopping workload gets between SIGTERM and force-kill

keys.default: (chart's global.tolerations, JSON — the runtime's own tolerations)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON array of toleration objects stamped onto every SPAWNED Pod's spec so a bare `kubectl run` bot/agent Pod (not a Deployment child) tolerates the same taints the runtime does — else it strands Pending forever on an all-tainted pool (#673). Empty [] ⇒ no tolerations; malformed JSON is fatal at spawn (a silently dropped constraint is the bug)

keys.default: (chart's global.nodeSelector, JSON — the runtime's own nodeSelector)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON object of node-label selectors stamped onto every SPAWNED Pod's spec so a bare `kubectl run` bot/agent Pod schedules onto the same pool the runtime does. Empty {} ⇒ no selector; malformed JSON is fatal at spawn (#673)

keys.default: (unset — the meeting-bot class declares no cpu, preserving runtime.v1's optional resources)
keys.description: k8s backend: CPU cores every SPAWNED meeting-bot Pod declares. runtime.v1 carries one value per dimension, so it sets BOTH the container's request and its limit (Guaranteed QoS) — the declaration a namespace ResourceQuota admits on (#1005). Unset/empty ⇒ no cpu declared (the pre-#1005 unbounded spawn); a non-numeric value is fatal at boot

keys.default: (unset — the meeting-bot class declares no memory, preserving runtime.v1's optional resources)
keys.description: k8s backend: memory (MiB) every SPAWNED meeting-bot Pod declares, as BOTH request and limit. A HARD ceiling — a bot exceeding it is OOM-killed mid-meeting — so size it for real meetings, not for the smallest node. Unset/empty ⇒ no memory declared; a non-numeric value is fatal at boot (#1005)

keys.default: (unset — the agent-worker class declares no cpu, preserving runtime.v1's optional resources)
keys.description: k8s backend: CPU cores every SPAWNED agent-worker Pod declares, as BOTH request and limit. Sized INDEPENDENTLY of the meeting bot — a code harness is not a browser — so an operator can right-size each class alone (#1005). Unset/empty ⇒ no cpu declared; a non-numeric value is fatal at boot

keys.default: (unset — the agent-worker class declares no memory, preserving runtime.v1's optional resources)
keys.description: k8s backend: memory (MiB) every SPAWNED agent-worker Pod declares, as BOTH request and limit. Unset/empty ⇒ no memory declared; a non-numeric value is fatal at boot (#1005)

keys.default: (unset — meeting-bot Pods take the runtime-wide RUNTIME_K8S_NODE_SELECTOR)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON object of node labels every SPAWNED meeting-bot Pod selects. When set it replaces the runtime-wide RUNTIME_K8S_NODE_SELECTOR for this class only, so bots can run on their own pool. Read and validated at boot (label keys and values per Kubernetes' rules); malformed is fatal at boot. Never taken from a workload spec

keys.default: (unset — meeting-bot Pods take the runtime-wide RUNTIME_K8S_TOLERATIONS)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON array of toleration objects (key, operator Equal|Exists, value, effect, tolerationSeconds) every SPAWNED meeting-bot Pod carries. When set it replaces the runtime-wide RUNTIME_K8S_TOLERATIONS for this class only. Validated at boot; malformed is fatal at boot. Never taken from a workload spec

keys.default: (unset — no priorityClassName, the cluster's default priority)
keys.description: k8s backend: the PriorityClass every SPAWNED meeting-bot Pod names. Validated at boot as a Kubernetes object name; Kubernetes' own system-* classes are refused. Never taken from a workload spec

keys.default: (unset — no imagePullSecrets on the Pod; the namespace's default ServiceAccount still applies its own)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON array of Secret names (or {"name": …} objects) every SPAWNED meeting-bot Pod pulls its image with. Validated at boot. Never taken from a workload spec

keys.default: (unset — agent-worker Pods take the runtime-wide RUNTIME_K8S_NODE_SELECTOR)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON object of node labels every SPAWNED agent-worker Pod selects. When set it replaces the runtime-wide RUNTIME_K8S_NODE_SELECTOR for this class only. Validated at boot; malformed is fatal at boot. Never taken from a workload spec

keys.default: (unset — agent-worker Pods take the runtime-wide RUNTIME_K8S_TOLERATIONS)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON array of toleration objects every SPAWNED agent-worker Pod carries. When set it replaces the runtime-wide RUNTIME_K8S_TOLERATIONS for this class only. Validated at boot; malformed is fatal at boot. Never taken from a workload spec

keys.default: (unset — no priorityClassName, the cluster's default priority)
keys.description: k8s backend: the PriorityClass every SPAWNED agent-worker Pod names. Validated at boot; Kubernetes' own system-* classes are refused. Never taken from a workload spec

keys.default: (unset — no imagePullSecrets on the Pod; the namespace's default ServiceAccount still applies its own)

keys.default: (unset — the profile's own: none for a meeting bot)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON array of the Linux capabilities every SPAWNED meeting-bot container keeps; all others are dropped and privilege escalation is off either way. Validated at boot (capability names; SYS_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE and the like refused). Never taken from a workload spec

keys.default: (unset — the profile's own: CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, FSETID, KILL, SETGID, SETUID, what a root worker needs to give the model's tools a user of their own)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON array of the Linux capabilities every SPAWNED agent-worker container keeps; all others are dropped. Set [] where the platform admits no added capability (OpenShift's restricted SCC, whose workers run non-root and do not use them). Validated at boot. Never taken from a workload spec

keys.default: (unset — the container runtime's default profile, under which a bot's browser runs without Chromium's sandbox)
keys.description: k8s backend: a Localhost seccomp profile every SPAWNED meeting-bot container runs under, as a path relative to the kubelet's seccomp root (the chart installs runtime_kernel/seccomp-userns.json at vexa/seccomp-userns.json and sets this, so the bot's Chromium can build its sandbox). Validated at boot (a plain relative path). Never taken from a workload spec

k8s backend: a Localhost seccomp profile every SPAWNED agent-worker container runs under instead of RuntimeDefault, as a path relative to the kubelet's seccomp root. Validated at boot. Never taken from a workload spec

k8s backend: true lets a spawned Pod's tolerations (runtime-wide or per class) include one with no key (it tolerates every taint) or one for a control-plane or system taint (node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, node-role.kubernetes.io/master, CriticalAddonsOnly). Off, such a value is refused at boot

DOCKER-HOST path (NOT an in-container path) to a claude credentials JSON (~/.claude/.credentials.json); the docker backend bind-mounts it READ-ONLY into every spawned agent-worker at /root/.claude/.credentials.json — the claude-code runner's subscription credential path. compose also mirror-mounts it into the runtime container at /var/lib/vexa/host-claude-credentials so the config.v1 file probe can verify the host file actually exists (docker turns a MISSING host path into an empty directory in the worker → 'Model inference failed: Not logged in'). PAIR IT WITH HOST_CLAUDE_DIR: this single-FILE mirror is pinned to the inode it was created with, so it goes stale the moment the CLI refreshes the token

keys.default: (unset — only the legacy single-file mirror is available)
keys.description: DOCKER-HOST path of the claude config DIRECTORY (~/.claude), mirror-mounted READ-ONLY into the long-lived runtime + agent-api containers at /var/lib/vexa/host-claude. Same credential as HOST_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS, delivered in the shape that SURVIVES A TOKEN REFRESH: the CLI replaces .credentials.json via rename(2) (a NEW inode), and a single-FILE bind stays pinned to the inode it was created with, so a long-lived container reads the pre-refresh token until it is recreated (32h of 'Not logged in' on the dogfood stack, 2026-08-31). A DIRECTORY bind resolves the filename live. Set it to the parent of HOST_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS

DOCKER-HOST path to Codex subscription auth (~/.codex/auth.json); mounted read-only into spawned agent workers at /tmp/.codex/auth.json (WORKER_CODEX_HOME), or copied to ~/.codex/auth.json in a process-backend child's private HOME
API-key credential path, brokered into spawned workers (alternative to the subscription mount)
